newsitem.title: ITALY: INSTANT VIEW - Italy June CPI 1.5 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Italy June CPI 1.5 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Following are economists' reactions to the estimated 1.5 percent rise in Italian June year-on-year consumer prices following data released by five sample cities on Friday.

The month on month rate was seen at 0.1 percent after a month on month rise of 0.3 percent in May and a year on year rate of 1.6 percent. Economists had forecast on average a year-on-year rate of 1.5/1.6 percent for June.
Bruno Rovelli, chief economist at Citibank in Milan, said: "This data should be pretty reassuring. But there is some risk of re-acceleration in the second half of the year."

A further six sample Italian cities, Turin, Venice, Bologna, Perugia, Naples and Palermo, release their data on Monday June 23, while statistics institute Istat will announce the final June figures on July 4.
Rovelli said: "I don't think the Bank of Italy is very much concerned right now about current inflation but clearly looking forward to what will happen in the second half of the year."

Marco Pianelli, economist at Nomura in London, said: "Even if inflation is very modest at the moment, it is bottoming out, you are not going to get any more falls in inflation (over the summer). So the idea is whether the Bank of Italy will keep rates (stable) for such a long time.

"I think there is an odd chance for (Bank of Italy governor) Antonio Fazio to surprise the market with a modest 50 basis points on Monday and then leave it unchanged for the rest of the year," he said. The official discount rate is 6.75 percent.

Alessandro Fugnoli, head of research at Caboto here, said: "It's more likely the Bank of Italy will wait for the third quarter at the end of September, when welfare reforms have been approved by government coalition parties."

Rovelli said: "Fazio is waiting for developments on (fiscal policy) which are not going to come soon but he's also waiting for underlying inflation in the second half of the year and what will happen with projected value added tax increases which should come through in October or at the latest in January 1998."
